invariants.expression: x >= 0 && x < width && y >= 0 && y < height
invariants.rationale: The assignment to cells[x][y] only happens if the indices are within proper bounds.

invariants.expression: x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height || cells[x][y] == cell
invariants.rationale: If assignment is performed (valid bounds), then cells[x][y] is set to cell; otherwise the assignment is skipped.

invariants.expression: x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height || cell == null || cells[x][y] == null || cells[x][y].equals(cell)
invariants.rationale: If cell is null or equals previous value, cells[x][y] will match what was passed.

invariants.expression: x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height || cells != null
invariants.rationale: cells must be non-null to store into cells[x][y] (structural invariant).

invariants.expression: x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height || (cells.length > x && cells[x].length > y)
invariants.rationale: The cells array must be large enough to accommodate x and y if assignment is performed.
